summary: Makio Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Otani University by 2009. He later held posts at Otani University, attested as an assistant professor (助教) from 2010 to 2012 and attested again in 2022.

Makoto Funaoka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University from around 1965 to 1974 and served as a professor at Hokkai-Gakuen University from circa 1988 to 2014.

Makoto Nagai was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1904 to 1907. He held positions at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1942) and Toyo University (~1943–1954), and taught Giyu Nishi.

Makoto Nagamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology who studied at Azabu Junior and Senior High School. He served as a professor at Japan Women's University from around 1989 to 2017.

Makoto Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral coursework at Waseda University around 1993 to 1999 and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 2003.

Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Harvard (~1975–1980) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held faculty posts at Harvard (~1980–1990, ~1998–2002) and Boston University (~1990).

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1955–1964). He held a post at Otani University from around 2000 to 2008 and taught Benjamin Brose.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University (attested 2003) and Secretary of the Asiatic Society. He also taught Reeta Bhattacharya.

Manfred Mayrhofer was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein. He held posts at Würzburg (~1958–1963), Saarland (~1963–1966), Vienna (~1966–1988), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Manfred Steger is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under Robert Aitken and at Rutgers University (~1991–1995). He held a post at RMIT University from around 2003 to 2012.
Manfred Taube was a Tibetologist who studied under Friedrich Weller from around 1947 to 1957. In 1991, he held a professorship in Central Asian studies at Leipzig University.

Manshi Kiyozawa was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Toyo University, and at the University of Tokyo (graduated 1887) under Ernest Fenollosa. He founded the Philosophical Society of Japan and served as president of Otani University (~1901–1903).
Manudeva is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under traditional teacher Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa and was a disciple of Bāla Śarman Pāyaguṇḍe.

Marc Aurel Stein was a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, educated in Vienna, Leipzig, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included Principal of Oriental College, Lahore, and Superintendent in the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2016 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst, and also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Matthew T. Kapstein as well as Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Granet was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études, Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, INALCO, and Collège de France.

Marcel Mauss was a scholar of religious studies and other fields who studied at the University of Bordeaux (~1890–1895). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1942).

Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris and under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She held a post at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1926–1967).

Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard (attested 2017). He also studied under Khenpo Dondrub Namgyal.
